target_customer: Players of browser-based strategy and social games
problem: Hardcore strategy games were scarce as accessible browser titles in the casual-dominated market of 2007.
business_model: Free-to-play browser games with in-game purchases

founders.name: Matt Maroon
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as Founder/Owner; no bio found. Seedtable says the company was formerly Draftmix.

technical_complexity.rationale: Persistent multiplayer strategy servers with real-time fleet battles is moderate engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Player communities in persistent worlds give some stickiness, but game genres are easy to imitate.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; the company remains small and later relaunched Starfleet Commander as SFC2.

market_need_then: 2007 industry reports describe a casual-games boom of about 200 million monthly players, leaving strategy genres less served, but no source states specific demand evidence for this company.

branding.brand_signature: Starfleet Commander title as the main brand asset

brand_strength.rationale: Studio name is generic and little press about it was found; the Starfleet Commander game carries more recognition than the studio.

pivots.why: Not stated; Seedtable says the company was formerly known as Draftmix.

outcome_analysis: Blue Frog Gaming, an Akron, Ohio studio behind the browser game Starfleet Commander, joined YC in Summer 2007 and a 2010 Series A of about 1.25M is reported by one database. The company still operates and relaunched the game as SFC2, so the CB Insights Dead label looks wrong. Little is public about its trajectory, so no success or failure story can be sourced.
notes: The 2010 Series A (1.25M, David Parker, Langley Steinert, YC) rests on a single database, CB Insights; another listing says 2M from Boston investors, unverified. CB Insights lists status Dead while YC lists Active and the game site is live; exit none. Competition: only present-day aggregator lists (Zynga, Making Fun) were found, nothing dated near 2007, so the list is empty. The YC page links a Crunchbase profile called draftmix.
